Row names y must match rownames(x). following commands simulate small survival dataset signal first two features construct lambda grid. linear predictor involves first two features , stable selection procedure expected recover . model fitted 40 bootstrap replicates random-permutation artificial features. output lists selected feature names, followed six features largest stability importances. small sample size FDR threshold saturates 1, selection set can empty; planted features g1 g2 instead recovered sorted importances, expected rank top. stability path makes comparison visible: sparse end lambda grid planted features lift away null background, saturated end every curve approaches FDR upper bound (dashed line 1).

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: Multinomial outcomes use named factor y. stability matrix one row per feature, importances aggregate across classes. following commands simulate three-class problem weak class signal first feature fit multinomial model. printed vector contains features selected multinomial fit. class signal confined feature m1, feature expected appear among selections.
code: n <- 90 p <- 12 ids <- paste0("s", seq_len(n)) x_multi <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p), nrow = n,   dimnames = list(ids, paste0("m", seq_len(p))) ) y_multi <- factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE), levels = c("A", "B", "C")) names(y_multi) <- ids # Weak class signal from first feature x_multi[y_multi == "B", 1] <- x_multi[y_multi == "B", 1] + 1.5 x_multi[y_multi == "C", 1] <- x_multi[y_multi == "C", 1] - 1.5  lambda_multi <- auto_lambda_grid(x_multi, y_multi, family = "multinomial", n_lambda = 6)  fit_multi <- stabl_fit(   x               = x_multi,   y               = y_multi,   lambda_grid     = lambda_multi,   family          = "multinomial",   n_bootstraps    = 30L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state    = 1L )  get_feature_names(fit_multi) #> character(0)

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: several rows belong subject batch, groups vector passed bootstrap resampling keeps whole groups together. prevents leakage across related samples. following commands simulate four repeated measurements per subject, inspect one grouped subsample draw, fit grouped model. call unique(groups[idx]) prints subjects entering one subsample; subject appears either four rows . final line reports number features selected grouped Gaussian fit. fixed hard_threshold = 0.5 used selection set non-empty: ten candidates, default data-driven threshold can legitimately select nothing, make similarity comparisons next section vacuous. Group labels forwarded stabl_multiomic_train_validate() (argument groups_train) stabl_multiomic_cv() (argument groups) outer fold construction. Classification bootstraps redraw subsamples least two observations per class present. slightly biases subsample distribution relative vanilla STABL; deviation deliberate documented, buys class-diverse subsamples.
code: n <- 48 p <- 10 ids <- paste0("s", seq_len(n)) groups <- setNames(rep(paste0("subj", seq_len(12)), each = 4), ids) x_grp <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p), nrow = n,   dimnames = list(ids, paste0("f", seq_len(p))) ) y_grp <- setNames(rnorm(n) + 0.5 * x_grp[, 1], ids)  # Inspect one grouped draw (whole subjects only) — this is what # sample_groups does internally for every bootstrap resample boot_subjects <- sample(unique(groups), 6L) idx <- which(groups %in% boot_subjects) unique(groups[idx]) #> [1] "subj2"  "subj7"  "subj8"  "subj10" "subj11" "subj12"  lambda_grp <- auto_lambda_grid(x_grp, y_grp, family = "gaussian", n_lambda = 6)  fit_grp <- stabl_fit(   x               = x_grp,   y               = y_grp,   sample_groups   = groups,   lambda_grid     = lambda_grp,   family          = "gaussian",   n_bootstraps    = 25L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   hard_threshold  = 0.5,   random_state    = 3L )  length(get_feature_names(fit_grp)) #> [1] 10

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: Selection-stability metrics compare feature lists repeated STABL runs. Jaccard similarity simplest overlap measure, adjusted similarity corrects chance overlap set sizes differ. Two fits different random states compared first, pairwise similarity matrix across four seeds computed afterwards. first two printed values Jaccard adjusted similarity selections seeds 11 22. matrix end gives pairwise Jaccard similarities fits seeds 11 14; -diagonal values close 1 indicate selections robust random state. matrix easier compare heatmap.
code: run_once <- function(seed) {   stabl_fit(     x = x_grp, y = y_grp, sample_groups = groups,     lambda_grid = lambda_grp,     family = "gaussian",     n_bootstraps = 20L,     artificial_type = "random_permutation",     hard_threshold = 0.5,     random_state = seed   ) }  fit_a <- run_once(11L) fit_b <- run_once(22L) sel_a <- get_feature_names(fit_a) sel_b <- get_feature_names(fit_b)  stabl_similarity(sel_a, sel_b) #> [1] 1 stabl_similarity(sel_a, sel_b, method = "adjusted", n_universe = ncol(x_grp)) #> [1] 0  # Pairwise matrix across several seeds fits <- lapply(11:14, run_once) sels <- lapply(fits, get_feature_names) stabl_similarity(sels, method = "jaccard", as_matrix = TRUE, remove_diag = TRUE) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1    1    1 #> [2,]    1    1    1 #> [3,]    1    1    1 #> [4,]    1    1    1 # Keep the full square matrix (remove_diag = FALSE) so both axes carry the # seed labels; as.table() on the diagonal-removed matrix would mislabel the # second axis with row indices instead of seed ids. jm <- stabl_similarity(sels, method = "jaccard", as_matrix = TRUE) dimnames(jm) <- list(seed_a = as.character(11:14), seed_b = as.character(11:14)) jm_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(jm)) names(jm_df) <- c("seed_a", "seed_b", "jaccard") ggplot2::ggplot(jm_df, ggplot2::aes(seed_a, seed_b, fill = jaccard)) +   ggplot2::geom_tile() +   ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(     label = sprintf("%.2f", jaccard)   )) +   ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey90") +   ggplot2::labs(x = "random_state", y = "random_state",                 title = "Selection overlap across repeated fits") +   ggplot2::theme_minimal()

title: Metacell aggregation: STABL on pooled single-cell expression
text: Single-cell measurements sparse noisy individual-cell level. Metacell methods partition cells small, homogeneous neighbourhoods pool counts, trading cellular resolution matrix smaller, denser, less zero-inflated (Baran et al., 2019, Genome Biology 20:206; Persad et al., 2023, Nature Biotechnology 41:916). Dedicated tools exist — metacell (Tanay lab) SEACells — pooling concept simple, STABL step downstream identical regardless metacells built. vignette therefore constructs metacells transparent, dependency-free greedy k-nearest-neighbour partition runs stabl_fit() pooled matrix. demonstration uses public 10x Genomics PBMC 3k data set asks: genes reliably distinguish monocyte lineage cells samples metacells rather single cells?

code: library(stablr) fixture_dir <- system.file("extdata", "pbmc3k", package = "stablr") counts   <- readRDS(file.path(fixture_dir, "pbmc3k_counts_hvg.rds")) clusters <- readRDS(file.path(fixture_dir, "pbmc3k_clusters.rds")) keep <- clusters != "c9" counts   <- counts[keep, ] clusters <- droplevels(clusters[keep])  lib <- Matrix::rowSums(counts) xn  <- log1p(1e4 * counts / lib)   # CP10k + log1p dim(xn) #> [1] 2689 1200

title: Metacell aggregation: STABL on pooled single-cell expression
text: embed cells 30 principal components grow metacells greedily: walking cells PC1 order, unassigned cell seeds metacell 24 nearest unassigned neighbours, every metacell reaches target size 25 cells; final partial neighbourhood merged nearest existing metacells. partition deterministic given seed.
code: pc <- prcomp(as.matrix(xn), rank. = 30)$x d  <- as.matrix(dist(pc)) n  <- nrow(pc) k  <- 25L assigned <- rep(NA_integer_, n) mc <- 0L for (i in order(pc[, 1])) {   if (!is.na(assigned[i])) next   pool <- which(is.na(assigned))   if (length(pool) < 2L * k) break   # leave the tail for merging   mc <- mc + 1L   assigned[pool[order(d[i, pool])[1:k]]] <- mc } left <- which(is.na(assigned)) for (i in left) {   idx <- which(!is.na(assigned))   assigned[i] <- assigned[idx[which.min(d[i, idx])]] } table(table(assigned)) #>  #> 25 26 27 28 29 30 31 32  #> 94  4  2  1  1  1  2  1

title: Metacell aggregation: STABL on pooled single-cell expression

code: mc_counts <- as.matrix(Matrix::fac2sparse(factor(assigned)) %*% counts) mc_xn     <- log1p(1e4 * mc_counts / rowSums(mc_counts))  maj <- tapply(clusters, assigned, function(v) {   tb <- table(v)   c(names(which.max(tb)), max(tb) / length(v)) }) mc_lab <- factor(vapply(maj, `[`, character(1L), 1L)) purity <- as.numeric(vapply(maj, `[`, character(1L), 2L)) table(mc_lab) #> mc_lab #> c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7 c8  #> 13 13 22 19  7  6 24  2 sum(purity < 0.6)   # impure metacells dropped #> [1] 15 keepmc <- purity >= 0.6

title: Reliability diagnostics, validation, and final models
text: stabl_diagnose() takes fitted "stabl_fit" returns machine-readable reliability report: warning_codes headline field: entry stable, machine-readable string naming specific concern (example flat boundary-hugging FDP+ curve, tie-heavy score distributions, low effective decoy count), downstream code can branch without parsing prose. empty vector means concern fired — guarantee validity. Two fields carry detail: cutoff block discloses conventions FDP+ estimate relies — selection rule (fdp_plus_minimum), comparator (strictly greater), exact denominator formula plus-one offset zero-real guard; threshold_path walks full threshold grid per-threshold selected counts FDP+ estimates, saturation boundary probes warning_codes summarize. evidence profile (d$evidence_profile) places fit’s learner x decoy x outcome x dimensionality regime calibration benchmarks — context interpretation, binary safe/unsafe verdict. Read calibration_scope trusting single number: FDP+ minimum stochastic-bound diagnostic, calibrated estimate realized FDP, low minimum curve “controlled FDR” (plot-reading article develops distinction).
code: d <- stabl_diagnose(fit) d$warning_codes #> [1] "STABL_DIAG_TIED_MINIMA"           "STABL_DIAG_FLAT_MINIMUM"          #> [3] "STABL_DIAG_BOUNDARY_MINIMUM"      "STABL_DIAG_HIGH_SCORE_DEPENDENCE" #> [5] "STABL_DIAG_EMPTY_SUPPORT" d$cutoff #> $selected_threshold #> [1] 1 #>  #> $selection_rule #> [1] "fdp_plus_minimum" #>  #> $hard_threshold #> NULL #>  #> $fdr_min_threshold #> [1] 1 #>  #> $comparator #> [1] "strictly greater (>)" #>  #> $denominator #> $denominator$artificial_proportion #> [1] 1 #>  #> $denominator$formula #> [1] "(n_artificial / artificial_proportion + 1) / pmax(1, n_real)" #>  #> $denominator$plus_one_offset #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $denominator$zero_real_guard #> [1] "pmax(1, n_real)" head(d$threshold_path) #>   threshold n_real n_artificial prop_real prop_artificial fdp_plus #> 1      0.00      8            8         1               1    1.125 #> 2      0.01      8            8         1               1    1.125 #> 3      0.02      8            8         1               1    1.125 #> 4      0.03      8            8         1               1    1.125 #> 5      0.04      8            8         1               1    1.125 #> 6      0.05      8            8         1               1    1.125 d$calibration_scope #> [1] "The FDP+ minimum is a stochastic-bound diagnostic, not a calibrated estimate of realized FDP (F-001). On pure-null designs the minimizing rule still selected 18-33 features with realized FDP 0.92-0.93 while reporting 0.42-0.66 (audit Phase 6, F-P6-1): an empty support is the only outcome a null dataset cannot produce by this rule." #> [2] "Calibration is regime-dependent in both directions (audit Phase 6, F-P6-2): approximately calibrated for knockoff decoys on independent signal, anti-conservative for permutation decoys, conservative under block correlation. Asking global permutation supplying block structure error: Every replicate seed derived replayably seed, null check exactly reproducible.
code: nv <- stabl_null_check(   x, y,   design = "independent",   fit_spec = list(n_bootstraps = 10,                   artificial_type = "random_permutation"),   n_reps = 5, seed = 7 ) nv$p_any_selection #> [1] 0 stabl_null_check(   x, y,   design = "independent",   blocks = rep(1:3, each = 20),   fit_spec = list(n_bootstraps = 10),   n_reps = 2, seed = 7 ) #> Error: #> ! design = "independent" applies a GLOBAL permutation of the outcome, which is not exchangeable under block/cluster structure. Use design = "within_block" or design = "whole_cluster", or drop the structure only if you can defend sample independence.

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: stabl_scores Numeric matrix (features \(\times\) lambdas) stability scores real features. stabl_scores_artificial Numeric matrix (artificial features \(\times\) lambdas) stability scores injected noise features. artificial_proportion Positive numeric scalar; fraction artificial features relative real features (used \(\pi\)). fdr_threshold_range Numeric vector threshold values sweep. Default: seq(0, 0.99, = 0.01), matching Python STABL's np.arange(0., 1., .01).

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: Named list: FDRs Numeric vector FDP+ estimates, one per threshold. min_fdr Minimum FDP+ achieved across threshold range. fdr_min_threshold Threshold value achieving min_fdr, capped 1. fdrs_table Numeric matrix (lambdas \(\times\) thresholds) per-lambda FDP+ values.

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: FDP+ threshold \(\tau\) estimated : $$\widehat{\text{FDP}}(\tau) =   \frac{(1/\pi) \cdot |\{j : \hat{q}_j^{\text{art}} > \tau\}| + 1}        {\max(1,\, |\{j : \hat{q}_j > \tau\}|)}$$ \(\pi\) artificial_proportion, \(\hat{q}_j\) maximum--lambda stability scores real feature \(j\), \(\hat{q}_j^{\text{art}}\) scores artificial feature \(j\).

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: Exceedance counts use strict > comparator: feature whose score equals threshold exactly counted.  matches Python STABL reference implementation part parity contract; "fix" >=.  several thresholds tie minimum FDP+, first (lowest) threshold grid wins, matching Python's argmin first-index semantics.  min_fdr decoy-based diagnostic (stochastic upper bound exchangeability artificial features), controlled FDR guarantee; exceeds 1, fdr_min_threshold capped 1 downstream selection yields empty support.

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
code: # Small synthetic stability-score matrices (3 real + 3 artificial features, # 2 lambda values) scores_real <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.6, 0.1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.05), nrow = 3) scores_art  <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.15, 0.25, 0.1), nrow = 3) result <- compute_fdp_plus(scores_real, scores_art,                            artificial_proportion = 1.0) result$min_fdr           # minimum FDP+ estimate #> [1] 0.5 result$fdr_min_threshold # threshold that achieves it #> [1] 0.3

title: Group-Aware Bootstrap Sampler Indices — group_bootstrap_indices
text: y Outcome vector length groups. groups Vector group identifiers (length y).  Values may type supports unique() equality comparison. n_subsamples Positive integer; target number rows subsample.  actual count may differ slightly due whole-group granularity (whole groups always preserved; realised count smallest group-aligned value >= n_subsamples). replace Logical; may group sampled ? Default FALSE. stratify Logical; TRUE, sample whole groups within outcome strata realised subsample retains class representation group structure permits .  group must map exactly one outcome class.  Whole groups still preserved, realised counts can exceed per-class targets.  Default FALSE. strata Optional categorical stratification design.  Provide vector one stratification factor, data.frame/matrix/list joint design across multiple factors.  group must map exactly one realised stratum. random_state Optional integer; seed used draw.  function clobber caller's global RNG state: previous .Random.seed restored exit (via withr::local_seed()). seed Deprecated; use random_state instead.  supplied, deprecation warning emitted value used random_state latter NULL.  removed future release.

title: Group-Aware Bootstrap Sampler Indices — group_bootstrap_indices
text: group-level sampling prevents leakage: individual rows subject appear bootstrap subsample complement, stability score becomes inflated learner can partially memorise subject-level patterns.  sampling complete groups, subsample "holdout" subject-disjoint, preserving independence assumption underlying STABL's FDP+ diagnostic assumptions. groups sampled: Groups drawn one time (without replacement default) running tally included rows reaches exceeds n_subsamples.  Whole groups always kept intact: last added group causes count exceed n_subsamples, surplus rows trimmed.  guarantees strongest leakage prevention (subsample complement always group-disjoint), cost slightly variable subsample size.  replace = TRUE group may drawn multiple times (useful groups). Degenerate bootstrap guard: sample_bootstrap_indices(), final subsample contains one unique class function retries class-diverse sample obtained.

title: Build an Adaptive Lasso Learner Adapter — make_adaptive_lasso_adapter
text: Adaptive lasso improves standard lasso assigning stronger penalties features small initial coefficients (likely noise) weaker penalties features large initial coefficients (likely signal). asymmetric penalisation achieves oracle property regularity conditions, selecting true support reliably plain lasso signal features moderate large effect sizes. Weights defined : $$w_j = 1 / (|\hat\beta_j^{\mathrm{init}}| + \epsilon)^\gamma$$ \(\hat\beta_j^{\mathrm{init}}\) comes ridge regression bootstrap subsample.  epsilon floor avoids division zero features near-zero ridge coefficients. adapter factory primarily internal backend used stabl_fit(). end--end feature selection workflows, prefer base_learner = "adaptive_lasso" stabl_fit().

title: Build an Adaptive Lasso Learner Adapter — make_adaptive_lasso_adapter
code: if (requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(2L)   x <- matrix(rnorm(200L), 20L, 10L)   y <- rnorm(20L)   adapter <- stablr:::make_adaptive_lasso_adapter(family = "gaussian", gamma = 1, epsilon = 1e-6)   mask <- adapter(x, y, data.frame(lambda = 0.1))   cat("selected:", sum(mask), "of", ncol(x), "features\n") } #> selected: 7 of 10 features

title: Dispatcher for Artificial Feature Generation — make_artificial_features
text: x Numeric matrix predictors (samples \(\times\) features). Must columns n_injected random permutation; knockoffs, constructor failure (e.g., rank-deficient input) governed knockoff_fallback: default ("stop") error, knockoff_fallback = "allow" fallback random permutation attempted. Fixed-X knockoffs require row augmentation also fail (fall back "allow") augmented knockoff rows aligned original outcome. knockoff modes fail closed 3 000 predictors; random permutation dimensional limit. n_injected Positive integer; number artificial columns append. Typically round(ncol(x) * artificial_proportion) computed stabl_fit(). type Character string; one "random_permutation", "knockoff", "knockoff_equi", "knockoff_mvr". random_state Optional integer; passed set.seed() random operations reproducibility.  NULL leaves RNG unchanged. Seeding happens exactly dispatcher; downstream generators inherit seeded RNG state re-seed (audit M-5). knockoff_fallback Character; fallback policy knockoff constructor fails supported-dimensional input (audit A1, strict fallback policy).  "stop" (default) raises error: knockoff--random-permutation fallback silently changes FDP+ calibration target, permutation features support FDP+ calibration.  "allow" restores pre-0.2.2 behavior (warn fall back random-permutation features affected chunk; fallback_history provenance records event).  benign knockoff_mvr -> knockoff_equi fallback unaffected: model-X constructions valid FDP+ calibration, remains warning either policy.

title: Dispatcher for Artificial Feature Generation — make_artificial_features
text: Named list three elements: x_augmented Numeric matrix size (nrow(x)) \(\times\) (ncol(x) + n_injected) artificial columns appended original features. noise_col_indices Integer vector length n_injected containing 1-based indices original x columns (artificial block) identify source features used build artificial column.  Used stabl_fit() look sparse-group-lasso group memberships artificial block via .append_noise_groups. artificial_provenance Additive metadata describing requested artificial-feature type, actual_type used scientific classification, generator modes used selected artificial columns, ordered structured fallback_history. Per-chunk counts reasons remain available 0.1.x compatibility.

title: Dispatcher for Artificial Feature Generation — make_artificial_features
text: Injecting artificial features supports STABL's FDP+ diagnostic calibration: mixing known-noise columns predictor matrix alongside real features, STABL can empirically estimate often variable pure noise selected given stability threshold.  observed noise-selection rate drives FDP+ estimate computed compute_fdp_plus(). current rule chooses minimum imply universal error-rate control. Four noise strategies supported: "random_permutation" Copies n_injected randomly chosen real columns shuffles copy independently, breaking signal preserving marginal distributions.  Fast broadly applicable. "knockoff" Generates fixed-X knockoffs via knockoff::create.fixed(), preserve second-moment (Gram) structure original design input's scale: t(xk) xk = t(x) x t(x) xk = t(x) x - diag(s) s >= 0 (0.2.2 scale contract).  Kept backward compatibility; note fixed-X knockoffs generated full design, exchangeability survive row subsampling bootstrap loop — prefer "knockoff_equi" "knockoff_mvr" correlation structure matters. "knockoff_equi" Generates model-X equicorrelated knockoffs via knockoff::create.gaussian(..., method = "equi").  matches GaussianSampler(method='equicorrelated') call Python STABL parity-correct knockoff type cross-language comparisons. "knockoff_mvr" Generates model-X MVR (minimum-variance- reconstructability) knockoffs.  S-matrix solved solve_mvr() (R-native port knockpy.mrc); sampling uses knockoff::create.gaussian(..., diag_s = S).  novel feature exclusive stablr.

title: Build a Random-Forest Learner Adapter (Calibrated, Scoped) — make_ranger_adapter
text: Permutation importance, Gini.  Gini importance biased towards high-cardinality features; permutation importance better-studied choice null calibration (Boruta likewise builds mean-decrease-accuracy). Pair model-X knockoff artificial features.  random forest multivariate learner: real null features correlated true signals receive leaked importance, permuted null features (artificial_type = "random_permutation") reproduce leakage, FDP+ estimate anti-conservative.  Model-X knockoff nulls ("knockoff_equi" / "knockoff_mvr") preserve correlation structure statistically sound pairing.  Combining base_learner = "rf" artificial_type = "random_permutation" stabl_fit() emits package warning effect. Calibrated within measured scope (WS-2).  knockoff_equi decoys mean empirical FDP 0.025 (linear design) 0.065 (low-dimensional nonlinear design), meeting predeclared criterion; met p = 50 strong correlation (0.44) binary outcomes (0.26).  Simulation evidence, guarantee.

title: Print STABL Selection Diagnostics — print.stabl_diagnostics
code: set.seed(1) x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8,             dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:8))) y <- setNames(x[, 1] * 2 + rnorm(60), rownames(x)) fit <- stabl_fit(x, y, n_bootstraps = 20, lambda_grid = "auto",                  artificial_type = "random_permutation") print(stabl_diagnose(fit)) #> STABL selection diagnostics #>   learner: lasso | family: gaussian | decoys: random_permutation #>   features: 8 real / 8 artificial | lambdas: 23 | bootstraps: 20 #>   selection rule: fdp_plus_minimum | threshold: 1 | comparator: strictly greater (>) #>   FDP+ minimum: 1.12 at threshold 0 (95 minimizing thresholds) #>   evidence: #>     - [empirically_concerning] lasso x random_permutation x gaussian (sparse independent, linear signal, low dimension) #>     - [empirically_concerning] lasso x any x gaussian (pure null (no signal)) #>     - [validated_in_stablr] lasso x any x gaussian (block-correlated AR(0.6), weak signal, n=100 (Phase 6 D3 conditions)) #>   warning codes: #>     - STABL_DIAG_TIED_MINIMA #>     - STABL_DIAG_FLAT_MINIMUM #>     - STABL_DIAG_BOUNDARY_MINIMUM #>     - STABL_DIAG_HIGH_SCORE_DEPENDENCE #>     - STABL_DIAG_EMPTY_SUPPORT #>   assumption notes: #>     - The first FDP+ minimum lies at the edge of fdr_threshold_range; consider widening the range before trusting the minimum. #>     - Mean absolute score-profile correlation among real features is 0.79: features co-select across the regularization path. Interpret per-feature selection cautiously; this probe does not by itself invalidate the decoy design. #>   calibration scope: #>     - The FDP+ minimum is a stochastic-bound diagnostic, not a calibrated estimate of realized FDP (F-001). On pure-null designs the minimizing rule still selected 18-33 features with realized FDP 0.92-0.93 while reporting 0.42-0.66 (audit Phase 6, F-P6-1): an empty support is the only outcome a null dataset cannot produce by this rule. #>     - Calibration is regime-dependent in both directions (audit Phase 6, F-P6-2): approximately calibrated for knockoff decoys on independent signal, anti-conservative for permutation decoys, conservative under block correlation. No single interpretation of the FDP+ minimum is safe across regimes.

title: Classic Bootstrap Sampler Indices — sample_bootstrap_indices
text: STABL accumulates often feature selected across many bootstrap subsamples; subsamples must drawn consistently avoid bias. function centralises sampling class-imbalance handling "degenerate bootstrap" guard (see ) applied uniformly. Class weighting: class_weights supplied sample's inclusion probability proportional weight class.  useful imbalanced binary multi-class outcomes unweighted subsampling frequently produce single-class bootstraps. Degenerate bootstrap guard: drawn subsample contains one unique class full outcome contains least two, function retries (without seed) class-diverse subsample found.  prevents downstream model failures classifiers require least two classes.

code: set.seed(42) n <- 50L p <- 10L x <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p),   nrow = n,   dimnames = list(paste0("s", seq_len(n)), paste0("f", seq_len(p))) ) y <- setNames(0.8 * x[, 1] - 0.5 * x[, 2] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), rownames(x)) lambda_grid <- data.frame(lambda = seq(0.02, 0.30, length.out = 4L))  # Default lasso path fit_lasso <- stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   n_bootstraps = 6L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 1L ) get_feature_names(fit_lasso) #> [1] "f1" "f2"  # Adaptive lasso path fit_adaptive <- stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   base_learner = "adaptive_lasso",   adaptive_gamma = 1.0,   adaptive_epsilon = 1e-6,   n_bootstraps = 6L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 2L ) get_importances(fit_adaptive) #>        f1        f2        f3        f4        f5        f6        f7        f8  #> 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.5000000 0.8333333 0.8333333 0.3333333 0.6666667 0.6666667  #>        f9       f10  #> 0.3333333 0.5000000   # Sparse-group lasso path (optional dependency) if (requireNamespace("sparsegl", quietly = TRUE)) {   feature_groups <- rep(seq_len(5L), each = 2L)   fit_sgl <- stabl_fit(     x = x,     y = y,     lambda_grid = lambda_grid,     base_learner = "sparse_group_lasso",     feature_groups = feature_groups,     n_bootstraps = 5L,     artificial_type = "random_permutation",     random_state = 3L   )   get_support(fit_sgl) } #>    f1    f2    f3    f4    f5    f6    f7    f8    f9   f10  #>  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE   # Multinomial path with three classes y_multi <- setNames(   factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE)),   rownames(x) ) fit_multi <- suppressWarnings(stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y_multi,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   family = "multinomial",   n_bootstraps = 5L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 4L )) get_feature_names(fit_multi) #> [1] "f1" "f2" "f3" "f4" "f5" "f6" "f8" "f9"

code: set.seed(3L) ids <- paste0("s", 1:18) y <- setNames(factor(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 6L)), ids) signal <- stats::model.matrix(~ y - 1) x <- matrix(   rnorm(18 * 6, sd = 0.3), 18, 6,   dimnames = list(ids, paste0("g", 1:6)) ) x[, 1:3] <- x[, 1:3] + signal nested <- suppressWarnings(stabl_multiomic_nested_cv(   x_list = list(rna = x), y = y,   candidates = list(list(name = "rna", blocks = "rna")),   lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.2, 0.1)),   outer_v = 3L, inner_v = 3L, n_bootstraps = 3L,   artificial_type = NULL, hard_threshold = 1e-9,   sample_fraction = 1, random_state = 3L )) nested$performance$balanced_error_rate #> [1] 0.2222222  # Study-disjoint folds: each block of four samples is treated as one # study; outer CV is leave-one-study-out. set.seed(4L) ids2 <- paste0("s", 1:20) y2 <- setNames(factor(rep(c("A", "B"), times = 10L)), ids2) x2 <- matrix(   rnorm(20 * 6, sd = 0.3), 20, 6,   dimnames = list(ids2, paste0("g", 1:6)) ) x2[, 1:2] <- x2[, 1:2] + stats::model.matrix(~ y2 - 1) study_labels <- setNames(rep(paste0("study", 1:5), each = 4L), ids2) nested2 <- suppressWarnings(stabl_multiomic_nested_cv(   x_list = list(rna = x2), y = y2,   candidates = list(list(name = "rna", blocks = "rna")),   lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.2, 0.1)),   outer_v = 5L, inner_v = 2L, n_bootstraps = 3L,   artificial_type = NULL, hard_threshold = 1e-9,   sample_fraction = 1, random_state = 4L,   study_labels = study_labels )) nested2$fold_scheme #> [1] "study_disjoint" nested2$outer_folds[[1L]]$study_ids #> [1] "study5"

title: Similarity Between Feature Sets — stabl_similarity
text: x Either character/integer vector selected feature identifiers (y must also supplied result single scalar), list vectors, one per STABL run (y must NULL pairwise similarities computed). y NULL (default) character/integer vector selected feature identifiers.  Supply y scalar mode, list x pairwise mode — . method Character; one "jaccard" (default), "adjusted", "pearson". n_universe Integer; total number candidate features universe (.e. number columns original predictor matrix). Required method = "adjusted" method = "pearson"; ignored method = "jaccard". as_matrix Logical; pairwise mode .  FALSE (default), returns \(N (N - 1) / 2\) -diagonal upper-triangle values flat vector row-major order (matching Python convention).  TRUE, returns full symmetric \(N \times N\) matrix. remove_diag Logical; used as_matrix = TRUE.  TRUE self-similarity diagonal removed row-wise, yielding \(N \times (N - 1)\) matrix row \(\) contains similarities run \(\) every run.

title: Similarity Between Feature Sets — stabl_similarity
text: scalar mode, numeric scalar.  pairwise mode as_matrix = FALSE, numeric vector length \(N (N - 1) / 2\). pairwise mode as_matrix = TRUE, numeric matrix dimension \(N \times N\) (\(N \times (N - 1)\) remove_diag = TRUE). matrix diagonal holds self-similarity set: exactly 1 "jaccard" "pearson", computed self-value "adjusted" (\(1 - k / d\) set size \(k \le d / 2\)), 1 construction measure chance-corrected.

title: Similarity Between Feature Sets — stabl_similarity
text: Three methods available: "jaccard" (default) Set-overlap fraction \(|\cap B| / |\cup B|\).  interpretable measure; correct chance overlap expected small large sets.  sets empty value 0 (convention matching Python implementation). "adjusted" Chance-corrected overlap, analogous Cohen's kappa sets: $$S_{\text{adj}}(, B) =       \frac{r - \mathbb{E}[r]}{\min(k_1, k_2) - \max(0, k_1 + k_2 - d)}$$ \(r = |\cap B|\), \(k_i = |A_i|\), \(d =\) n_universe, \(\mathbb{E}[r] = k_1 k_2 / d\).  Returns 0 either set empty equals full universe. "pearson" Pearson-correlation-inspired chance correction (phi coefficient): $$S_{\text{Pearson}}(, B) =       \frac{r - k_i k_j / d}{d \cdot \upsilon_i \upsilon_j}$$ \(\upsilon_i = \sqrt{\pi_i (1 - \pi_i)}\) \(\pi_i = k_i / d\).  Returns 1 sets empty equal universe; 0 exactly one .

title: Similarity Between Feature Sets — stabl_similarity
code: # Scalar mode: two sets stabl_similarity(c("A", "B", "C"), c("B", "C", "D"))                # 0.5 #> [1] 0.5 stabl_similarity(c("f1", "f2", "f3"), c("f2", "f3", "f4"),                  method = "adjusted", n_universe = 10L) #> [1] 0.3666667  # Pairwise mode: a list of sets, one per run sets <- list(c("f1", "f2", "f3"), c("f2", "f3", "f4"), c("f1", "f3", "f5")) stabl_similarity(sets)                                        # flat vector #> [1] 0.5 0.5 0.2 stabl_similarity(sets, as_matrix = TRUE)                      # 3 x 3 #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]  1.0  0.5  0.5 #> [2,]  0.5  1.0  0.2 #> [3,]  0.5  0.2  1.0 stabl_similarity(sets, as_matrix = TRUE, remove_diag = TRUE)  # 3 x 2 #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]  0.5  0.5 #> [2,]  0.5  0.2 #> [3,]  0.5  0.2 stabl_similarity(sets, method = "adjusted", n_universe = 10L) #> [1] 0.36666667 0.36666667 0.03333333

what: API changes (2026-10-21, Phase 14 PR-B: redundant families merged)
title: stablr 0.3.0.9000 (development)
text: Three redundant function families merged single entry points mixOmics style small verb-based API. ten historical names remain exported deprecated shims — one .Deprecated() warning per call, legacy argument names mapped silently — removed 1.0.0. shims excluded pkgdown reference index; man pages remain reachable via ?name. Similarity (8 -> 2): stabl_similarity() unifies scalar pairwise similarity method = "jaccard" (default), "adjusted", "pearson": two vectors give scalar, list sets gives flat row-major upper-triangle vector (Python convention), as_matrix = TRUE returns full symmetric matrix (remove_diag = TRUE drops diagonal row-wise). stabl_similarity_summary() reduces pairwise values median/mean statistic spread measure. shims jaccard_similarity(), jaccard_similarity_matrix(), adjusted_similarity(), adjusted_similarity_pairwise(), adjusted_similarity_summary(), pearson_similarity(), pearson_similarity_pairwise(), pearson_similarity_summary() forward two new functions.
